title: Ensure that the SharePoint Central Administration Site is TLS- enabled
description: Transport Layer Security (TLS) provides protection when communicating over the internet. Traffic is encrypted for portions of information transportation. Ensure that the Central Administration site is configured to be used with TLS. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure that the SharePoint Central Administration Site is TLS- enabled

audit.command: In IIS Manager select 'SharePoint Central Administration v4' > Bindings. Verify an HTTPS binding exists with Port, Host name and a valid SSL certificate set (and no plain HTTP binding is used). Get-SPWebApplication -IncludeCentralAdministration shows the CA URL.

remediation.command: Acquire a certificate, then Set-SPCentralAdministration -Port <port> -SecureSocketsLayer; if the certificate is for an FQDN: Set-SPAlternateUrl -Identity https://servername:443 -Url https://fqdn:443 -Zone Default; bind the certificate in IIS.

title: Ensure the SharePoint farm service account (database access account) is configured with the minimum privileges for the local server.
description: The SharePoint farm service account (database access account) must be configured with the minimum privileges for the local server. Prints the number of local groups on this server, other than WSS_RESTRICTED_WPG, WSS_ADMIN_WPG and WSS_WPG, that directly contain the farm service account (expected 0). Only direct membership is evaluated; nested domain groups need manual review. Run on every farm server. Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure the SharePoint farm service account (database access account) is configured with the minimum privileges for the local server.

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $acct = "$((Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction Stop).DefaultServiceAccount.Name)"; if ($acct -notmatch '\\') { throw 'farm account not found' }; $dom, $sam = $acct.Split('\', 2); $re = '/' + [regex]::Escape($dom) + '/' + [regex]::Escape($sam) + '$'; $allowed = @('WSS_RESTRICTED_WPG','WSS_ADMIN_WPG','WSS_WPG'); $pc = [ADSI]("WinNT://" + $env:COMPUTERNAME + ",computer"); $bad = @($pc.Children | Where-Object { $_.SchemaClassName -eq 'group' } | Where-Object { $allowed -notcontains "$($_.Name)" } | Where-Object { $paths = @($_.Invoke('Members') | ForEach-Object { $_.GetType().InvokeMember('ADsPath', 'GetProperty', $null, $_, $null) }); @($paths | Where-Object { $_ -match $re }).Count -gt 0 }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Remove the farm account from every local group except WSS_RESTRICTED_WPG, WSS_ADMIN_WPG and WSS_WPG (Server Manager > Local Users and Groups, or Remove-LocalGroupMember -Group <group> -Member <DOMAIN\farmaccount>), and remove any other rights/services assigned to it.

title: Ensure the SharePoint setup account is configured with the minimum privileges in Active Directory.
description: The SharePoint setup account must be configured with the minimum privileges in Active Directory. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Ensure the SharePoint setup account is configured with the minimum privileges in Active Directory.

audit.command: In Active Directory Users and Computers open the SharePoint setup account > Member Of. Verify it is a member of Domain Users only, and that no other delegated rights, services or permissions are assigned to it.

remediation.command: Remove the setup account from every AD group other than Domain Users and remove any additional delegated permissions.

title: Ensure the SharePoint setup account is configured with the minimum privileges on the SQL server.
description: The SharePoint setup account must be configured with the minimum privileges on the SQL server. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure the SharePoint setup account is configured with the minimum privileges on the SQL server.

audit.command: In SQL Server Management Studio on the farm's SQL instance open Security > Logins > <SharePoint setup account> > Server Roles. Verify only dbcreator and securityadmin are checked (plus public). sysadmin or other roles are non-compliant.

remediation.command: In SSMS > Security > Logins > setup account > Server Roles, check only dbcreator and securityadmin (ALTER SERVER ROLE <role> DROP MEMBER [DOMAIN\setup] for others).

title: Ensure the SharePoint farm service account (database access account) is configured with the minimum privileges on the SQL server.
description: The SharePoint farm service account (database access account) must be configured with the minimum privileges on the SQL server Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5 Ensure the SharePoint farm service account (database access account) is configured with the minimum privileges on the SQL server.

audit.command: In SQL Server Management Studio on the farm's SQL instance open Security > Logins > <farm service account> > Server Roles. Verify only dbcreator and securityadmin are checked (plus public). Get-SPFarm | Select DefaultServiceAccount shows the account.

remediation.command: In SSMS > Security > Logins > farm account > Server Roles, check ONLY dbcreator and securityadmin (ALTER SERVER ROLE <role> DROP MEMBER [DOMAIN\farm] for others).

title: Ensure the SharePoint Central Administration site is not accessible from Extranet or Internet connections
description: The SharePoint central administration site should be configured so that its ports and interfaces are not accessible to untrusted external or internet connections. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7 Ensure the SharePoint Central Administration site is not accessible from Extranet or Internet connections

audit.command: Determine the Central Administration port (stsadm -o getadminport from %CommonProgramFiles%\Microsoft Shared\Web Server Extensions\16\BIN, or Get-SPWebApplication -IncludeCentralAdministration). Verify in the firewall rules that this server/port is not reachable from the Internet, extranet or other external connections.

remediation.command: Configure perimeter and host firewalls so the Central Administration port is reachable only from internal administrative networks.

title: Ensure that SharePoint specific malware (i.e. anti-virus) protection software is integrated and configured
description: SharePoint-specific malware (i.e. anti-virus) protection software must be integrated and configured. Prints compliant when the farm antivirus settings scan documents on upload and download and attempt to clean infected documents. A SharePoint-integrated antivirus product must also be installed for the settings to take effect. Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.5 Ensure that SharePoint specific malware (i.e. anti-virus) protection software is integrated and configured

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $av = [Microsoft.SharePoint.Administration.SPWebService]::ContentService.AntivirusSettings; if ($null -ne $av -and $av.UploadScanEnabled -eq $true -and $av.DownloadScanEnabled -eq $true -and $av.CleaningEnabled -eq $true) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Install a SharePoint-integrated antivirus product, then Central Administration > Security > Manage antivirus settings: select Scan documents on upload, Scan documents on download and Attempt to clean infected documents.

title: Ensure that the SharePoint Central Administration interface is not hosted in the DMZ.
description: The SharePoint Central Administration site should not be installed onto the network DMZ, which is exposed to external internet connections. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.11 Ensure that the SharePoint Central Administration interface is not hosted in the DMZ.

audit.command: Note the Central Administration URL (e.g. http://server:port) on an admin workstation, then try to open it from a workstation or server in the DMZ. Finding if it is reachable from the DMZ or if a server hosting Central Administration is in the DMZ.

remediation.command: Remove Central Administration from DMZ servers: run the SharePoint Products Configuration Wizard, choose Do not disconnect from the server farm, then Yes, I want to remove the website from this machine.

title: Ensure Anonymous authentication is denied
description: SharePoint web applications should be configured to disallow anonymous authentication, which would allow users to authenticate and use the applications without confirming their identity. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Ensure Anonymous authentication is denied

audit.command: Central Administration > Manage web applications > select each web application > Authentication Providers > each zone. Verify 'Enable anonymous access' is not selected. PowerShell aid: Get-SPWebApplication | % { $_.IisSettings.Values } | ? AllowAnonymous.

remediation.command: Authentication Providers > each zone: clear 'Enable anonymous access' and save. Repeat for each web application.

title: Ensure compilation or scripting of database pages via the PageParserPaths elements is not allowed
description: Allowing compilation or scripting of database pages via the "PageParserPaths" elements can lead to disclosure of compilation error messages containing server info and source code exposed to the user. Reads every local web application web.config (all zones) and prints the number of PageParserPath entries under SharePoint/SafeMode/PageParserPaths (expected 0). Run on each Web Front End; a missing web.config fails the audit. Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3 Ensure compilation or scripting of database pages via the PageParserPaths elements is not allowed

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $cfgs = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | ForEach-Object { $_.IisSettings.Values } | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $_.Path.FullName 'web.config' } | Sort-Object -Unique); if ($cfgs.Count -eq 0) { throw 'no web application web.config found' }; $bad = @($cfgs | ForEach-Object { [xml]$x = Get-Content -LiteralPath $_ -Raw -ErrorAction Stop; @($x.SelectNodes('/configuration/SharePoint/SafeMode/PageParserPaths/PageParserPath')) } | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Remove every <PageParserPath .../> element from <PageParserPaths> in each web application's web.config (leave the element empty), then recycle the application pool.

title: Ensure Farm Administrators group membership is restricted
description: Farm Administrators have full control over every server and site collection; membership must be limited to named administrators.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint Server Benchmark - Service accounts / Farm Administrators group (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: Central Administration > Security > Manage the farm administrators group: confirm only approved named admin accounts [and BUILTIN\Administrators if required] are members; no users, broad groups or service accounts other than the farm account. Also check Get-SPShellAdmin output and the local Administrators group on each farm server.

remediation.command: Remove unapproved members from the Farm Administrators group in Central Administration and with Remove-SPShellAdmin; document approved membership.

title: Ensure all web applications use HTTPS
description: Web applications served over HTTP expose credentials and authentication cookies. Prints the number of web applications whose URL is not HTTPS (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint Server Benchmark - Web applications / SSL (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.Url -notlike 'https://*' }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Extend or reconfigure each web application with an HTTPS binding and alternate access mapping (New-SPAlternateURL / Set-SPAlternateURL), bind a trusted certificate in IIS, then remove the HTTP zone.

title: Ensure web application pools do not run as the farm account
description: The farm account has full control of the configuration database; running content application pools as it means any web-tier compromise owns the farm. Prints the number of web applications whose pool identity is the farm account (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint Server Benchmark - Service accounts / Least privilege (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $farm = (Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction Stop).DefaultServiceAccount.Name; $bad = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.ApplicationPool.Username -eq $farm }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Register a dedicated managed account (New-SPManagedAccount) and move the application pool: $wa.ApplicationPool.CurrentIdentityType = 'SpecificUser'; $wa.ApplicationPool.Username = 'DOMAIN\svc-sp-apppool'; $wa.ApplicationPool.Update($true); $wa.ApplicationPool.Deploy().

title: Ensure access to SharePointEmailws.asmx is limited to only the server farm account
description: Restrict access to the Microsoft SharePoint Directory Management Service by securing the file associated with this service, which is SharePointEmailws.asmx. Only the SharePoint server farm account requires access. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure access to SharePointEmailws.asmx is limited to only the server farm account

audit.command: Open %CommonProgramFiles%\Microsoft Shared\Web Server Extensions\16\ISAPI\SharePointEmailws.asmx > Properties > Security (or run Get-Acl on it). Verify only WSS_RESTRICTED_WPG (the farm account) has Modify/Write access to the file.

remediation.command: Edit the file ACL so only WSS_RESTRICTED_WPG has modify access to SharePointEmailws.asmx; remove write/modify for other principals.

title: Ensure specific whitelisted IP addresses, IP address ranges, and/or domains are set
description: Access to the SharePoint web application should be restricted to a certain group of users. Typically, this is done through restricting IP addresses to selectively allow known and approved user populations. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure specific whitelisted IP addresses, IP address ranges, and/or domains are set

audit.command: In IIS Manager select the 'SharePoint Central Administration v4' site > IP Address and Domain Restrictions. Verify allow entries list only approved administrative IP addresses, ranges and/or domains, and that unlisted clients are denied.

remediation.command: IIS Manager > SharePoint Central Administration v4 > IP Address and Domain Restrictions > Add Allow Entry for each approved admin address/range; set the default for unspecified clients to Deny.

title: Ensure that the underlying Internet Information Services (IIS) Authentication module is set to use Kerberos as its Authentication Provider
description: The Kerberos protocol is a more secure protocol than NTLM and is based on ticketing. In this scheme, a user provides a valid user name and password to an authentication server. Then, the authentication server grants the user a ticket. The ticket can be used on the network to request network resources. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure that the underlying Internet Information Services (IIS) Authentication module is set to use Kerberos as its Authentication Provider

audit.command: For each SharePoint IIS site check the NTAuthenticationProviders / Windows Authentication providers (IIS Manager > Authentication > Windows Authentication > Providers, or appcmd/adsutil on legacy IIS). Verify Negotiate is listed (Negotiate,NTLM) so Kerberos is used; NTLM only (the default) is non-compliant.

remediation.command: Set the Windows Authentication providers of each SharePoint site to Negotiate,NTLM (IIS Manager > Authentication > Windows Authentication > Providers, or adsutil set w3svc/<id>/root/NTAuthenticationProviders Negotiate,NTLM) and register the required SPNs.

title: Ensure 'Blocked File Types' is configured to match the enterprise blacklist
description: A common tactic of malware is to identify the type of malicious code protection software running on the system and deactivate it. Malicious code includes viruses, worms, Trojan horses, and Spyware. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure 'Blocked File Types' is configured to match the enterprise blacklist

audit.command: Central Administration > Security > Define blocked file types. For each web application (Change Web Application), compare the blocked list with the enterprise file-type blacklist; every blacklisted extension must be present. ($wa.BlockedFileExtensions lists them in PowerShell.)

remediation.command: Central Administration > Security > Define blocked file types > select the web application > add each blacklisted extension (one per line) > OK. Repeat for every web application.

title: Ensure Dbcreator and Securityadmin roles are only used as needed
description: In certain situations, database administrators (DBAs) may want to operate independently from SharePoint 2016 administrators and create and manage all the databases. This is typical in IT environments where security requirements and company policies require a separation of administrator roles. The farm administrator provides SharePoint 2016 database requirements to the DBA, who then creates the... Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.8 Ensure Dbcreator and Securityadmin roles are only used as needed

audit.command: In SSMS Object Explorer > Security > Server Roles, open dbcreator and securityadmin > Properties > Members. Verify only the accounts that need these roles (SharePoint setup/farm accounts during provisioning) are members.

remediation.command: Remove members that do not need dbcreator or securityadmin (SSMS role Properties > Members, or ALTER SERVER ROLE dbcreator DROP MEMBER [login]).

title: Ensure SharePoint implements an information system isolation boundary that minimizes the number of non-security functions included within the boundary containing security functions.
description: Review the SharePoint server configuration to ensure an information system isolation boundary that minimizes the number of non-security functions included within the boundary containing security functions are implemented. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure SharePoint implements an information system isolation boundary that minimizes the number of non-security functions included within the boundary containing security functions.

audit.command: On the server hosting Central Administration open IIS Manager > Sites > SharePoint Central Administration v4 > Edit Bindings. Verify the site is bound to an out-of-band (management) or non-production IP address rather than all unassigned/production addresses.

remediation.command: IIS Manager > SharePoint Central Administration v4 > Edit Bindings: bind the site to an out-of-band (OOB) management IP address.

title: Ensure SharePoint implements security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.
description: SharePoint must implement security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure SharePoint implements security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.

audit.command: Finding if: the Central Administration server is in the DMZ; Central Administration can be reached from a production network without first connecting to the management VPN; or a remote desktop session to a SharePoint server can be opened from a production network without the management VPN.

remediation.command: Move Central Administration servers to an isolated management network segment reachable only via the management VPN.

title: Ensure SharePoint identifies data type, specification, and usage when transferring information between different security domains so policy restrictions may be applied.
description: SharePoint must identify data type, specification, and usage when transferring information between different security domains so policy restrictions may be applied. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure SharePoint identifies data type, specification, and usage when transferring information between different security domains so policy restrictions may be applied.

audit.command: Central Administration > Security > Configure information rights management. Finding if 'Do not use IRM on this server' is selected or a configuration error is shown (e.g. '... IRM will not work until the client is configured properly'). RMS must be located via AD or specified.

remediation.command: Central Administration > Security > Configure information rights management: select 'Use the default RMS server specified in Active Directory' or specify the RMS server; ensure 'Do not use IRM on this server' is not selected.

title: Ensure that SharePoint is configured with "Strict" browser file handling settings
description: SharePoint must prevent the execution of prohibited mobile code. Prints the number of web applications whose BrowserFileHandling is not Strict (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.6 Ensure that SharePoint is configured with "Strict" browser file handling settings

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { "$($_.BrowserFileHandling)" -ne 'Strict' }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Central Administration > Manage Web Applications > General Settings > Browser File Handling: Strict (or $wa = Get-SPWebApplication <url>; $wa.BrowserFileHandling = 'Strict'; $wa.Update()).

title: Ensure that SharePoint application servers are protected by a reverse proxy
description: A reverse proxy is server component that sits between the internet and the web servers. It accepts HTTPS requests, provides various services, and forwards the requests to one or many servers. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.9 Ensure that SharePoint application servers are protected by a reverse proxy

audit.command: Review the SharePoint architecture and network diagrams and verify all HTTPS requests from users reach the SharePoint servers only through a reverse proxy (no direct client access to the web front ends).

remediation.command: Deploy a reverse proxy that terminates/inspects all HTTPS requests and routes them to the SharePoint servers; block direct client access to the servers.

title: Ensure SharePoint database servers are segregated from application server and placed in a secure zone.
description: Segregating the SharePoint database server from the application server provides a layered defense architecture. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.10 Ensure SharePoint database servers are segregated from application server and placed in a secure zone.

audit.command: Review the SharePoint architecture and verify the SharePoint database server is segregated from the application servers and placed in a secure network zone, with only the required ports open from the application servers.

remediation.command: Move the SharePoint database server into a secure network zone and open only the specific ports required from the application servers.

title: Ensure claims-based authentication is used for all web applications and zones of a SharePoint 2019 farm
description: Claims-based authentication enables systems and applications to authenticate a user without requiring the user to disclose more personal information than necessary. SharePoint continues to offer support for both claims and classic authentication modes. Claims-based identity is an identity model in SharePoint that includes features such as authentication across users of Windows-based systems and... Prints the number of web applications not using claims-based authentication (UseClaimsAuthentication is not True) (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure claims-based authentication is used for all web applications and zones of a SharePoint 2019 farm

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.UseClaimsAuthentication -ne $true }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Convert classic-mode web applications to claims (SharePoint 2019: Convert-SPWebApplication -Identity <url> -From Legacy -To Claims -RetainPermissions after testing; the benchmark shows $wa.UseClaimsAuthentication = 1; $wa.Update()).

title: Ensure Windows Authentication uses Kerberos and not the NT Lan Manager (NTLM) authentication protocol
description: If Windows Authentication mechanisms are used on SharePoint, the system should be configured to use the Kerberos authentication protocol rather than the NT Lan Manager (NTLM) equivalent. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure Windows Authentication uses Kerberos and not the NT Lan Manager (NTLM) authentication protocol

audit.command: Central Administration > Manage web applications > Authentication Providers > each zone. Verify Integrated Windows authentication is checked with Negotiate (Kerberos) selected, not NTLM. (Get-SPAuthenticationProvider -WebApplication <url> -Zone <zone> shows DisableKerberos = False.)

remediation.command: Authentication Providers > zone: check Integrated Windows authentication and select Negotiate (Kerberos); register HTTP SPNs for the application pool accounts first.

title: Ensure that auditable events and diagnostic tracking settings within the SharePoint system is consistent with the organization's security plans
description: SharePoint must allow designated organizational personnel to select which auditable events are to be audited by specific components of the system. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure that auditable events and diagnostic tracking settings within the SharePoint system is consistent with the organization's security plans

audit.command: Central Administration > Monitoring > Configure diagnostic logging. Verify the selected event categories and event/trace levels match those defined in the organization's system security plan (Get-SPLogLevel lists them). Inconsistency is a finding.

remediation.command: Central Administration > Monitoring > Configure diagnostic logging: set event categories and trace levels to match the system security plan (or Set-SPLogLevel).

title: Ensure that remote sessions for accessing security functions and security-relevant information are audited
description: Remote access to SharePoint security functions (e.g., user management, audit log management, etc.) and security relevant information requires the activity be audited by the organization. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure that remote sessions for accessing security functions and security-relevant information are audited

audit.command: For each site collection subject to auditing: Settings > Site Settings > Site collection audit settings. Verify all events the organization requires to be audited (e.g. editing users and permissions, deleting/restoring items, security-relevant changes) are selected.

remediation.command: Site Settings > Site collection audit settings: select the events required by organizational policy and click OK, for each site collection in scope.

title: Ensure SharePoint is configured with HTTPS connections
description: By default, communication between Web servers and service applications within a farm takes place by using HTTP with a binding to TCP 32843. Configurations should be changed to enable SSL/TLS based HTTPS connections with a binding to TCP port 32844 instead. Prints the number of web service applications whose default endpoint listens on plain http (expected 0). Service applications without an HTTP-based endpoint are skipped. Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure SharePoint is configured with HTTPS connections

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPServiceApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.PSObject.Properties['DefaultEndpoint'] -and $null -ne $_.DefaultEndpoint } | Where-Object { @($_.DefaultEndpoint.ListenUris | Where-Object { $_.Scheme -eq 'http' }).Count -gt 0 }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Set-SPServiceApplication -Identity <service application> -DefaultEndpoint https (or Central Administration > Service Applications > select the application > Publish > choose https).

title: Ensure that SharePoint user sessions are terminated upon user logoff and when the idle time limit is exceeded
description: The SharePoint platform should be configured with a user session idle time limit of 15 minutes. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure that SharePoint user sessions are terminated upon user logoff and when the idle time limit is exceeded

audit.command: Central Administration > Application Management > Manage Web Applications > each web application > General Settings > Web Page Security Validation. Verify Security Validation is On and 'Security Validation Expires' is set to 15 minutes ($wa.FormDigestSettings shows Enabled/Expires).

remediation.command: General Settings > Web Page Security Validation: On, expires after 15 minutes (or $wa.FormDigestSettings.Enabled = $true; $wa.FormDigestSettings.Timeout = New-TimeSpan -Minutes 15; $wa.Update()).

title: Ensure that the SafeControls list is set to the minimum set of controls needed for your sites
description: The Safe Controls list contains the names of controls and Web Parts, specific to your SharePoint site, that server administrators can designate as safe for use on any .aspx page within a site. This list is part of the Web.config file in your Web application root. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2 Ensure that the SafeControls list is set to the minimum set of controls needed for your sites

audit.command: Open the web.config of each web application root and review the <SafeControls> section. Verify only SafeControl entries for approved, required assemblies/namespaces are present (each with Safe="True" only where needed); remove unused custom entries.

remediation.command: Remove SafeControl entries for assemblies that are not required (prefer deploying web parts via solution packages so entries are managed), keeping only the minimum set needed by your sites.

title: Ensure the SharePoint CallStack and AllowPageLevelTrace "SafeMode" parameters are set to false
description: The CallStack and PageLevelTrace parameters are used when debugging a problem and displays detailed additional information. Reads every local web application web.config (all zones) and prints the number of files whose SharePoint/SafeMode element does not have CallStack="false" and AllowPageLevelTrace="false" (expected 0). Run on each Web Front End. Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.4 Ensure the SharePoint CallStack and AllowPageLevelTrace "SafeMode" parameters are set to false

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $cfgs = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | ForEach-Object { $_.IisSettings.Values } | ForEach-Object { Join-Path $_.Path.FullName 'web.config' } | Sort-Object -Unique); if ($cfgs.Count -eq 0) { throw 'no web application web.config found' }; $bad = @($cfgs | Where-Object { [xml]$x = Get-Content -LiteralPath $_ -Raw -ErrorAction Stop; $sm = $x.SelectSingleNode('/configuration/SharePoint/SafeMode'); $null -eq $sm -or $sm.GetAttribute('CallStack') -ne 'false' -or $sm.GetAttribute('AllowPageLevelTrace') -ne 'false' }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: In each web application web.config set <SafeMode ... CallStack="false" AllowPageLevelTrace="false">, then save (IIS recycles the application).

title: Ensure self-service site creation is disabled
description: Self-service site creation lets any user create site collections, bypassing governance and permission review. Prints the number of web applications with it enabled (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint Server Benchmark - Web applications / Self-service site creation (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.SelfServiceSiteCreationEnabled -eq $true }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Central Administration > Application Management > Manage web applications > select web application > Self-Service Site Creation > Off (or $wa.SelfServiceSiteCreationEnabled = $false; $wa.Update()).

title: Ensure a separate organizational unit (OU) in Active Directory exists for SharePoint 2019 objects.
description: SharePoint 2019 includes an internal service, the Microsoft SharePoint Directory Management Service, for creating e-mail distribution groups. When you configure e-mail integration, you have the option to enable the Directory Management Service feature, which lets users create distribution lists. When users create a SharePoint group and they select the option to create a distribution list, the... Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6 Ensure a separate organizational unit (OU) in Active Directory exists for SharePoint 2019 objects.

audit.command: On a domain controller open Active Directory Users and Computers. Verify a separate OU exists used only for SharePoint 2019 objects, and that only the account used by the Microsoft SharePoint Directory Management Service has write access to that OU (Properties > Security / Advanced).

remediation.command: Create a dedicated OU for SharePoint 2019 objects and restrict write access on it to the SharePoint Directory Management Service account only.

title: Ensure that the SharePoint Online Web Part Gallery component is configured with limited access
description: For each SharePoint web application, the platform should be configured to prevent users from accessing the Online Web Part Gallery. Prints the number of web applications where users can access the Online Web Part Gallery (AllowAccessToWebPartCatalog is not False) (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.9 Ensure that the SharePoint Online Web Part Gallery component is configured with limited access

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPWebApplication -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.AllowAccessToWebPartCatalog -ne $false }); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Central Administration > Security > Manage web part security > for each web application select 'Prevents users from accessing the Online Web Part Gallery' (or $wa = Get-SPWebApplication <url>; $wa.AllowAccessToWebPartCatalog = $false; $wa.Update()).

title: Ensure a secondary SharePoint site collection administrator has been defined on each site collection.
description: A secondary SharePoint site collection administrator must be defined when creating a new site collection. Prints the number of site collections without a secondary site collection administrator (SecondaryContact empty) (expected 0). Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure a secondary SharePoint site collection administrator has been defined on each site collection.

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $bad = @(Get-SPSite -Limit All -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $sc = $_.SecondaryContact; $_.Dispose(); $null -eq $sc } ); $bad.Count

remediation.command: Central Administration > Application Management > Change site collection administrators > select each site collection > set the Secondary site collection administrator (or Set-SPSite <url> -SecondaryOwnerAlias DOMAIN\user).

title: Ensure that SharePoint is set to reject or delay network traffic generated above configurable traffic volume thresholds.
description: SharePoint must reject or delay, as defined by the organization, network traffic generated above configurable traffic volume thresholds. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.7 Ensure that SharePoint is set to reject or delay network traffic generated above configurable traffic volume thresholds.

audit.command: In IIS Manager, for each SharePoint site that receives user traffic open Advanced Settings > Connection Limits. Verify Connection Time-out, Maximum Bandwidth and Maximum Concurrent Connections each have a configured (non-default/limited) value.

remediation.command: IIS Manager > site > Advanced Settings > Connection Limits: set Connection Time-out, Maximum Bandwidth and Maximum Concurrent Connections for every user-facing SharePoint site.

title: Ensure that On-Premise SharePoint servers is configured without OneDrive redirection linkages.
description: Disable OneDrive Redirection for On-Premise SharePoint servers Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.8 Ensure that On-Premise SharePoint servers is configured without OneDrive redirection linkages.

audit.command: Central Administration > Office 365 > Configure OneDrive and Sites links. Verify the My Site URL field is empty so on-premises users are not redirected to OneDrive/SharePoint Online.

remediation.command: Central Administration > Office 365 > Configure OneDrive and Sites links: remove any URL from the My Site URL field and save.

title: Ensure SharePoint displays an approved system use notification message or banner before granting access to the system.
description: SharePoint web applications must display an approved system use notification message or banner before granting access. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure SharePoint displays an approved system use notification message or banner before granting access to the system.

audit.command: Obtain the list of web applications (Get-SPWebApplication), browse to each web application's home page and verify the approved system-use notification/warning banner is displayed before access is granted.

remediation.command: Configure every web application to show the approved warning banner at session start (e.g. a banner page referenced from global.asax that redirects back after acknowledgement); back up global.asax first.

title: Ensure that the SQL Server component to SharePoint is set to listen on non-default ports, with the defaults (UDP 1434 and TCP 1433) disabled
description: The default instance of SQL Server listens for client requests on TCP 1433. By default, client computers that connect to SQL Server first connect by using TCP 1433. If this communication is unsuccessful, the client computers query the SQL Server Resolution Service that is listening on UDP 1434 to determine the port on which the database instance is listening. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure that the SQL Server component to SharePoint is set to listen on non-default ports, with the defaults (UDP 1434 and TCP 1433) disabled

audit.command: On the SQL Server used by SharePoint open SQL Server Configuration Manager > SQL Server Network Configuration > Protocols for <instance> > TCP/IP > IP Addresses. Verify a non-default static TCP port is used (not 1433, no dynamic port) and that UDP 1434 / TCP 1433 are blocked (SQL Browser disabled or firewalled).

remediation.command: Set a non-default static TCP port for each IP (clear TCP Dynamic Ports), restart SQL Server, block TCP 1433/UDP 1434 in the firewall and configure a SQL client alias on the SharePoint servers.

title: Ensure that the MaxZoneParts setting for Web Parts is configured
description: Limit the number of web parts in SharePoint to a minimum value that is needed. Manual review.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint 2019 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.1 Ensure that the MaxZoneParts setting for Web Parts is configured

audit.command: On each Web Front End open the web.config of every SharePoint IIS site and find <WebPartLimits MaxZoneParts="50" PropertySize="1048576"/>. Verify MaxZoneParts is configured to the minimum value your pages require (default 50).

remediation.command: Edit web.config on every WFE: set <WebPartLimits MaxZoneParts="<minimum needed>" .../>, save, then run iisreset during a maintenance window.

title: Ensure diagnostic (ULS) logs are not stored on the system drive
description: ULS trace logs grow quickly; storing them on the system drive risks filling it and stopping the server, which also loses audit evidence. Run on a SharePoint farm server as a farm administrator; the audit loads the Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell snap-in and fails if it cannot.
reference: CIS Microsoft SharePoint Server Benchmark - Logging / Diagnostic logging configuration (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PSSnapin Microsoft.SharePoint.PowerShell -ErrorAction Stop }; if (-not (Get-Command Get-SPFarm -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'SharePoint cmdlets are not available' }; $c = Get-SPDiagnosticConfig -ErrorAction Stop; $loc = [Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables("$($c.LogLocation)"); if ($loc -and -not $loc.StartsWith($env:SystemDrive, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -and $c.LogMaxDiskSpaceUsageEnabled -eq $true) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-SPDiagnosticConfig -LogLocation 'D:\SPLogs\ULS' -LogMaxDiskSpaceUsageEnabled -LogDiskSpaceUsageGB 20 (the path must exist on every farm server).
